$comment: Phase-0 forensic style spec for the plan-visual-grammar campaign. MEASURED from vector operators in the qbiq reference PDF, not eyeballed and not pixel-sampled. This file is the pre-registration: 'looks professional' becomes 'matches these values within the stated tolerances', checkable per PR.

provenance.source: docs/reference/qbiq/extracted/Sample Report from Qbiq/Sample Report/Crystal Tower  Modern-2024-08-11-07-17-04.pdf
provenance.method: PyMuPDF get_drawings() / get_text('dict') read the PDF's own vector operators. Stroke widths and fill colours are EXACT values from the file, not samples of a rasterisation — no anti-aliasing error, no DPI conversion, no colour clustering. A 150-dpi render was used only for visual confirmation and background sampling.
provenance.method_deviation_from_brief: The brief specified 'render to PNG at known DPI, sample and cluster hex values, measure stroke widths in px'. The plan pages are VECTOR (3495-4080 drawing ops each), so reading the operators is strictly more accurate than sampling their rasterisation. Deviation is an improvement in precision, not a change of scope.
provenance.laiout_reference: ABSENT. No Laiout export exists in the repository. This is a QBIQ-ONLY spec. Per the brief, web marketing screenshots were NOT substituted.
brief_premises_corrected: The brief states the pack is in research/ and cites a prior research/qbiq-workbook-spec.json. Neither is true: the pack is in docs/reference/qbiq/, and no workbook spec exists in the repo. There was no prior spec to model this on.
'AI Space Planning Report.zip' and 'Sample Report from Qbiq.zip' contain the SAME PDF. There is exactly one qbiq plan document, giving three plan pages (Alternatives A/B/C).

findings_that_contradict_the_brief.$comment: Phase 0 exists to be believed over assumptions. Three brief assumptions are falsified by measurement. Each must be re-decided before the phase that depends on it.

wall_poche.brief_assumed: Phase 2a: 'Walls render as filled polygons at their real thickness, dark poche fill per spec' — described as the single highest-leverage change.
wall_poche.measured: There is NO dark poche anywhere in the reference. Walls are drawn as thin DOUBLE LINES with unfilled interiors: 463 paths per page at 0.2903 pt carry fill=None. The only heavy black strokes (1.0234 pt) are outlines of ZONE polygons whose fills are the pastel zone colours, i.e. enclosed-room boundaries — not poche.
wall_poche.consequence: Phase 2a as written would move DSource AWAY from the reference, not toward it. The high-leverage change is the WEIGHT HIERARCHY (2x wall over 1x furniture, 7x room enclosure), not fill. Needs an owner decision before 2a proceeds.

labels.brief_assumed: Phase 2d: 'Room labels become in-room text: name with area/pax beneath, centred in the pole of inaccessibility.'
labels.measured: The entire plan area contains 8 text spans at 4.35 pt — 'STOR.', 'COAT.', 'IT', 'CLEA.', 'WELL.' — abbreviations for SMALL SERVICE ROOMS ONLY. There are no room names, no areas, no seat counts anywhere in the drawing. All zone identification is carried by a LEGEND outside the plan (10.5 pt).
labels.consequence: qbiq's label grammar is legend-driven colour identification plus tiny abbreviations for rooms too small to read by colour. Implementing name+area+pax in every room would be MORE annotation than the reference, not less. Needs an owner decision before 2d proceeds.

zone_fill_lightness.brief_assumed: Phase 2e: 'the current full-strength blue circulation wash becomes a near-white tint'.
zone_fill_lightness.measured: qbiq fills are high-saturation, high-lightness PASTELS, not near-white: mean S 86.2%, mean L 85.7% (S range 28-100, L range 68.4-92.4). Only IT Room is genuinely muted (S 28.0%, L 68.4%).
zone_fill_lightness.consequence: 'Near-white' undershoots the reference. The correct target is L 80-92% at HIGH saturation — colour stays clearly readable; it is the LIGHTNESS that carries the quietness, not desaturation.

palette.$comment: Measured fill values. Per the brief's standing decision, DSource keeps its own HUES; these S/L levels are the discipline to adopt.

grid.measured: 0 of 394 sampled px non-white in an empty band

zone_fill_targets.$comment: THE ADOPTABLE RULE — apply to DSource hues.

saturation_pct.outlier_allowed: one muted service colour (IT Room) at S~28

line_weights.$comment: Exact PDF stroke widths in points. RATIOS are the portable contract; absolutes depend on the reference's page scale and should not be copied literally.
line_weights.hierarchy_summary: furniture 1x -> walls 2x -> room enclosure 7x. Openings are punched by overdrawing in WHITE at 8.5x, which is how the wall line breaks at a door.

provisional: role attribution for the 1.05x and 1.5x tiers — measured but their semantic use was not isolated

labels.content: room-type abbreviation only — no area, no pax, no full names
labels.applies_to: small service rooms only (storage, coat, cleaner, wellness, IT)
labels.primary_identification: LEGEND outside the plan, 10.5 pt, colour swatch + zone name

scale.derived: 1 pt paper = 0.308 ft real = ~93.8 mm real, i.e. roughly 1:266
scale.confidence: medium — unit is inferred from the report's imperial metrics, not stated on the drawing

tolerances.$comment: How conformance is checked in later phases. Scripted, not eyeballed.
tolerances.note: Palette tolerance applies to the S/L TARGETS, not to qbiq's hexes — DSource keeps its own hues by standing decision.
